source_text:
τοῖς ἀναξίοις διὰ τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας διδόμενα, τὸ δὲ τῆς ἀγάπης
κατόρθωμα τοῦ εὐσεβοῦς. τοῦτο οὖν λέγει· ποθεῖτε τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ κρείττονα. καὶ
ὁδὸν ὑμῖν δείκνυμι τὴν ἄγουσαν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὴν τῶν κρειττόνων χαρισμάτων
ἀπόλαυσιν, ὁδὸν δὲ τὴν ἀγάπην· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν νόμον πληροῖ. ὁ δὲ νόμον πληρῶν
εὐδοκιμεῖ. ὁ δὲ εὐδοκιμῶν λαμβάνει χάρισμα πνευματικόν. Ἐπειδὴ ἑώρα αὐτοὺς
ζηλοῦντας τοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ χαρίσματα, τὴν δὲ ἀγάπην οὐ θερμαίνοντας, διδάσκει ὡς
Korυφαιότατον ἀγαθὸν ἡ ἀγάπη· ἐκεῖνα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα ἐσθ' ὅτε καὶ ἀναξίοις
ἐδίδοτο διὰ τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας, τὸ δὲ τῆς ἀγάπης κατόρθωμα ἴδιόν ἐστι
τοῦ εὐσεβοῦς. ὁδὸν οὖν λέγει τὴν ἀγάπην τὴν ἄγουσαν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὴν τῶν κρειττόνων
ἀπόλαυσιν· τί γὰρ ἀνώτερον τοῦ χαρίσματος τῆς ἀγάπης τῆς πάντα πληρούσης τὸν
νόμον; 265 Καὶ τίς γλῶσσα ἀγγέλων, παρ' οἷς οὐ στῆθος, οὐ λάρυγξ, οὐ γλῶσσα, οὐ
φωνή; ἀλλ' ἐπειδή, ὡς λέγει Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ ∆ευτερονομίῳ, ἔστησεν ὁ θεὸς ὅρια
ἐθνῶν κατὰ ἀριθμὸν ἀγγέλων θεοῦ– τότε δὲ δηλαδὴ ἔστησεν, ὅτε εἰς γλώσσας
ἐμέρισεν τοὺς τὸν πύργον οἰκοδομεῖν ἐπιχειρήσαντας–· ἐπειδὴ γὰρ οὐκέτι ἀπὸ τῆς
ὁμοφωνίας ἐφυλάττοντο εἰς συμφωνίαν, ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ἠλλοτριώθησαν ἀλλήλων ταῖς
τῆς γλώσσης ἐναλλαγαῖς, ἐτέθησαν ἄγγελοι, ἵνα ἕκαστος φυλάσσῃ ὃ ἐπιστεύθη
ἔθνος, καὶ μηδὲν παραναλωθῇ καὶ ἀπόληται. διὰ τοῦτο ἀγγέλων γλώσσαις καλεῖ τὴν
διαφορὰν τῶν γλωσσῶν. δεῖ δὲ εἰδέναι ὅτι ὥσπερ ἄρτον ἀγγέλων λέγει ὁ ∆αυὶδ οὐχ
ὡς ἐσθιόντων, οὕτως καὶ ἀγγέλων γλώσσας οὐχ ὡς λαλούντων· ἐκεῖνό τε γὰρ καὶ
τοῦτο ὡς ὑπουργούντων τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διατάξει. ἀνθρώπων μὲν οὖν γλῶσσα ἡ
πεπαιδευμένη–ἐπείσακτος γὰρ αὕτη παρὰ τὴν φυσικὴν ἡ ἔντεχνος–, ἀγγέλων δὲ
γλῶσσα ἡ κατὰ φύσιν εἰς πολλὰ μερισθεῖσα. Γέγονα χαλκὸς ἠχῶν ἢ κύμβαλον
ἀλαλάζον. ἐντεῦθεν φαίνεται ὅτι ἀγγέλων λέγει τὴν ἐναλλαγὴν τῶν γλωσσῶν καὶ
τὴν διαφοράν· ὁ γὰρ λαλῶν ἄλλαις γλώσσαις παρὰ τοῖς οὐκ εἰδόσιν αὐτὰς ὥσπερ
κύμβαλόν ἐστι μόνον ἦχον ἀποτελοῦν, νόημα δὲ οὐδὲν ἐπιδεικνύμενον. Ἀνθρώπων
γλῶσσαν λέγει τὴν ῥητορικήν, γραμματικήν, φιλοσοφικήν, νοητικήν, συγγραφικήν,
τεχνικήν, συζητητικήν. ποία δὲ γλῶσσα παρ' ἀγγέλοις παρ' οἷς οὐ στῆθος, οὐ
φάρυγξ, οὐ φωνή, οὐκ ἄλλο τι σωματικόν; ἀγγέλων γλώσσας τὰς διαφορὰς τῶν
γλωσσῶν αἷς ἐπέστησαν οἱ ἄγγελοι κατὰ τὸ τῆς διασπορᾶς τῆς ἐπὶ τῆς πυργοποΐας,
ἵνα ἕκαστος φυλάττῃ ὃ ἐπιστεύθη ἔθνος. ὥσπερ δὲ ἄρτον ἀγγέλων νοοῦμεν τὸν διὰ
τῆς ἐπιταγῆς τῶν ἀγγέλων χορηγούμενον–οὐχ ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι ἤσθιον, ἀλλ' ὅτι οἱ
ἄγγελοι παρέχειν ἐπετάγησαν– οὕτως καὶ ἀγγέλων γλώσσας τὰς διαφορὰς τῶν
γλωσσῶν αἷς ἐπέστησαν ἄγγελοι. Χαλκοῦ δὲ ἦχον καὶ κυμβάλου ἀλαλαγμὸν τὰς
διαφορὰς τῶν γλωσσῶν εἶπεν· ὅταν γὰρ οὐκ οἶδέν τις τὰ ἐν ἑτέρᾳ γλώσσῃ
λαλούμενα, οὕτως ἔχει τὸν λαλοῦντα ὡς κύμβαλον ἄσημον ἀποτελοῦν, νόημα δὲ
οὐκ ἐμφαῖνον. 266 1 Kor 13,2 Μυστήριον λέγει πᾶν τὸ ἀγνοούμενον μέν, δυνάμει δὲ
πνεύματος ἀποκαλυπτόμενον. ἓν μυστήριόν ἐστι τοῦτο, ὡς καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ λέγει· οὐ
γὰρ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο καὶ πάλιν ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω. 1
Kor 13,4 Μετ' ὀλίγα διδάσκει τί ἐστιν ἀγάπη, ὅπου λέγει· ἡ ἀγάπη μακροθυμεῖ καὶ τὰ
ἑξῆς. διὸ ἄλλο ἐστὶ τὸ ἐλεεῖν καὶ ἕτερον τὸ ἀγαπᾶν, ὅμως καὶ τὸ δοῦναι τὴν οὐσίαν
πτωχοῖς καὶ τὸ ἐκδοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς μαρτύριον· ἐὰν μήπω τῆς ἀγάπης λόγῳ γίνηται,
λανθάνει εἰς κενοδοξίαν καὶ φιλοτιμίαν κενὴν ἐκπίπτον. διὸ εἰ καὶ μεταδώσομεν διὰ
τὴν περὶ τὸν λαμβάνοντα ἀγάπην, ἢ διὰ τὴν περὶ τὸν ἐντειλάμενον θεὸν
μεταδοτέον, καὶ εἰ μαρτυρήσομεν διὰ τὴν περὶ τὸν κύριον ἀγάπην, τοῦτο ἡμῖν
ὑπομενετέον. 1 Kor 13,8 Ἡ ἀγάπη οὐδέποτε ἐκπίπτει, τοῦτ' ἔστιν οὐδέποτε
ἐξολισθαίνει εἰς ἁμάρτημα. 1 Kor 13,10 Ἡ ἐκ μέρους καταργεῖται τῆς ὁλοκλήρου
γνώσεως δοθείσης· ὀλίγα γὰρ οἴδαμεν τῶν πλειόνων ἔτι λανθανόντων. 1 Kor 13,11–
12 Ὥσπερ, φησίν, ὅτε ἤμην παῖς, νηπίου εἶχον τοὺς λογισμούς, παρελθὼν δὲ εἰς
ἄνδρα τέλειον ἔσχον τὸν νοῦν, οὐκέτι ἁπλῶς εἰδὼς τὸν πατέρα ὅτι πατήρ, ἀλλὰ καὶ
κατὰ τί πατήρ ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ ὅτι γιγνώσκω νῦν ἐκ μέρους, τοῦτο ἐν καιρῷ τελείῳ
μαθήσομαι. καὶ ὅπερ νῦν ὡς ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ ἀμυδρῶς, τοῦτο ἐν καιρῷ ἐναργῶς
γνώσομαι. οὐκ εἶπεν δὲ «γνώσομαι τότε μυστήρια», ὅπερ ἀκόλουθον ἦν, ἀλλὰ
ἐπιγνωσθήσομαι· ὁ γὰρ ἐπιγνωσθεὶς παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἰκειωθεὶς αὐτῷ, οὗτος καὶ
τῆς αὐτοψίας τῶν μυστηρίων τυγχάνει. 1 Kor 13,13 Μήπω ἀποκαλυφθείσης ἡμῖν
πάσης γνώσεως, μένει ἡμῖν τὸ πιστεύειν ὅτι ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ἡμῖν πᾶσα γνῶσις.
pass_a_gloss: [12:31 note, column-2 form, continued] ...given also to the unworthy because of the building up of the church, but the achievement of love [is] of the devout one. So he says this: 'desire the greater gifts. And I show you a way', the one leading you to the enjoyment of the greater gifts, and the way is love; for the one loving fulfills law. And the one fulfilling law is approved. And the one approved receives a spiritual gift. [Other form] Since he saw them envying those having the gifts, but not warming love, he teaches that love is the topmost good. [Not printed again: for those gifts were sometimes given even to the unworthy because of the building up of the church, but the achievement of love is proper to the devout. So he calls love the way leading us to the enjoyment of the greater things; for what is higher than the gift of love, which fulfills the whole law?] [Page 265, no label; words of 13:1] And what tongue of angels, among whom there is no chest, no larynx, no tongue, no voice? But since, as Moses says in Deuteronomy, God set boundaries of nations according to the number of angels of God (and clearly he set [them] then, when he divided into languages those who attempted to build the tower); for since they were no longer kept into concord from sameness of speech, but were as it were estranged from one another by the changes of the language, angels were placed, so that each may guard the nation he was entrusted with, and nothing may be wasted and lost. Because of this he calls the difference of the languages tongues of angels. And one must know that as David says bread of angels not as of [angels] eating, so also tongues of angels not as of [angels] speaking; for both that and this [are said] as of [angels] serving God's ordinance. The tongue of men then is the educated one (for this artful one is imported beside the natural one), but the tongue of angels is the one by nature divided into many. 'I have become sounding brass or clanging cymbal.' From here it appears that he calls [tongues] of angels the change of the languages and the difference; for the one speaking in other tongues among those not knowing them is like a cymbal producing only sound, but showing no meaning. [Second form, printed as an addition] He calls tongue of men the rhetorical, grammatical, philosophical, intellectual, prose-writing, technical, disputational [tongue]. [Not printed again: And what tongue among angels, among whom no chest, no throat, no voice, nothing else bodily? [He calls] tongues of angels the differences of the languages over which the angels were set according to the dispersion at the tower-building, so that each may guard the nation he was entrusted with. And as we understand bread of angels as that supplied through the command of the angels (not that the angels ate, but that the angels were commanded to provide), so also tongues of angels [as] the differences of the languages over which angels were set. And he said the sound of brass and the clanging of the cymbal [of] the differences of the languages; for when someone does not know the things spoken in another language, he regards the speaker so, as a cymbal producing unclear [sound], but not showing meaning.] [Label 1 Kor 13,2] He calls mystery everything unknown but revealed by power of the Spirit. This is one mystery, as he says elsewhere too: 'for I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery', and again 'look, I tell you a mystery.' [Label 1 Kor 13,4] A little later he teaches what love is, where he says 'love is patient' and the rest. Therefore showing mercy is one thing and loving another; even giving one's property to poor people and giving oneself up to martyrdom, if it does not yet happen by reason of love, unnoticed falls out into vainglory and empty love of honor. Therefore if we share, it must be shared because of the love toward the receiver or because of the love toward God who commanded; and if we bear witness, this must be endured by us because of the love toward the Lord. [Label 1 Kor 13,8] Love never falls out, that is, never slips into sin. [Label 1 Kor 13,10] The [knowledge] in part is abolished when the whole knowledge has been given; for we know few things, the more still being hidden. [Label 1 Kor 13,11-12] As, he says, when I was a child I had the reasonings of an infant, but having passed into a perfect man I had the mind [of one], no longer knowing simply the father, that [he is] father, but also in what respect he is father, so also what I know now in part, this I will learn at the perfect time. And what [I see] now as in a mirror dimly, this I will know clearly in time. And he did not say 'I will then know mysteries', which was the consequence, but 'I will be known'; for the one known by God and made his own, this one also obtains the eyewitness sight of the mysteries. [Label 1 Kor 13,13] All knowledge not yet having been revealed to us, there remains for us to believe that all knowledge will be revealed to us.
pass_b_english: …to the unworthy for the building up of the church, but the achievement of love belongs to the devout. So this is what he says: “Earnestly desire the greater gifts. And I am showing you a way” (1 Corinthians 12:31) that leads you to the enjoyment of the greater gifts, and the way is love. The one who loves fulfills the law; the one who fulfills the law wins approval; the one who wins approval receives a spiritual gift.
The second catena form adds: He saw them envying those who had the gifts while their love stayed cold, so he teaches that love is the highest good of all.

On 1 Corinthians 13:1: And what tongue do angels have, when they have no chest, no larynx, no tongue, no voice? But Moses says in Deuteronomy that God set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God (Deuteronomy 32:8). He clearly set them at the time when he divided into languages those who had tried to build the tower. They were no longer kept in concord by a common speech; they had become strangers to one another, as it were, through the changes of language. So angels were appointed, each to guard the nation entrusted to him, so that none might be squandered and lost. That is why he calls the difference of languages “tongues of angels.” We should know that, just as David speaks of “bread of angels” (Psalm 78:25) not because angels eat, so he speaks of “tongues of angels” not because angels speak. Both are said because the angels serve God's ordering of things. The “tongue of men,” then, is the trained tongue, for the artful tongue is something brought in on top of the natural one. The “tongue of angels” is the natural tongue divided into many. “I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.” From this it is clear that by “of angels” he means the change and difference of languages. Someone who speaks in other tongues among people who do not know them is like a cymbal that makes only a noise and shows no meaning.
The second catena form adds: By “tongue of men” he means the language of rhetoric, grammar, philosophy, speculation, prose writing, the arts and debate.

On 1 Corinthians 13:2: By “mystery” he means anything that is unknown but revealed by the power of the Spirit. Each such thing is a mystery, as he says elsewhere, “For I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery” (Romans 11:25), and again, “Look, I tell you a mystery” (1 Corinthians 15:51).

On 1 Corinthians 13:4: A little further on he teaches what love is, where he says, “Love is patient,” and the rest. So showing mercy is one thing and loving is another. Even giving one's property to the poor and handing oneself over to martyrdom, if it is not yet done for love's sake, slips without our noticing into vainglory and empty ambition. So if we share, we must share out of love for the one who receives or out of love for God who commanded it; and if we bear witness, we must endure it out of love for the Lord.
On 1 Corinthians 13:8: “Love never fails”: that is, it never slips into sin.
On 1 Corinthians 13:10: What is partial is done away with when complete knowledge has been given. We know little now, and more still lies hidden.

On 1 Corinthians 13:11–12: When I was a child, he says, I had a child's way of reasoning, but when I grew to full manhood I had a man's understanding. I no longer knew simply that my father is my father, but also in what sense he is a father. In the same way, whatever I know in part now, I will learn at the time of completion; and what I grasp now only dimly, as in a mirror, I will then know clearly. He did not say, “Then I will know mysteries,” which would have been the natural sequel, but “I will be known.” The one who is known by God and made his own is the one who also gains the sight of the mysteries with his own eyes.
On 1 Corinthians 13:13: Since not all knowledge has yet been revealed to us, what remains for us is to believe that all knowledge will be revealed to us.

choices.why: Severianus reads the passive and argues from it; translated as he reads, not as the printed New Testament text.

choices.english: “Love never fails”: that is, it never slips into sin
choices.why: Severianus glosses ἐκπίπτει as ἐξολισθαίνει εἰς ἁμάρτημα.
Septuagint wording, which the argument needs; same verse as KJV Deuteronomy 32:8.
Kind of trained speech in a list with rhetoric, grammar, philosophy; 'of the intellect'.

choices.english: Each such thing is a mystery
choices.why: Read as distributive after πᾶν τὸ ἀγνοούμενον.

choices.english: form printed first kept; the other only where it adds
choices.why: Brief rule on doublets; here the column-2 form stands first in the copy-text.
